- FinLytics targets (from today): p95 end-to-end latency <= 350ms, p99 <= 600ms for single-turn text generation on 2k token context.
- Typical concurrency target: sustained 200 concurrent requests, burst to 400 for short windows.
- Throughput: ~1.5M tokens/day, with peak token rate ~1200 tok/s.
- Streaming requirement: client expects token-by-token streaming with max time between tokens <= 150ms during generation.

Action items:

2) We'll run a quick hosted vs your current provider comparison for p95/p99 (end-to-end, inc. network) and share results by Monday.

Thanks Marissa — confirmed on the numbers with a couple clarifications: 

- The p95/p99 targets are end-to-end as measured from our web client, so they include network time to the provider and the provider response time.
- For long-running generations (>= 750 tokens) we expect streaming to start within 300ms and then maintain <150ms between tokens. For short responses (<250 tokens) the p95 target is tighter: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms.
- Concurrency: the 200 sustained is per-region. We have clients in US-East and US-West; peak across both is expected to hit 400 concurrently but often not at the same millisecond.

We appreciate Redwood running the hosted comparison. One ask: can you run tests from both us-east and us-west and include a synthetic client that simulates our browser RTTs (US-East ~35ms, US-West ~55ms)?

Thanks — Alex

Thanks for the ping — quick technical notes based on the numbers: 

- Baseline hosted config to run: 1x A10G-like instance (GPU), inference engine with continuous batching disabled for strict latency, token parallelism off, KV cache primed. If we need to push p99 below 600ms at 2k context, we should evaluate dedicated capacity (multi-GPU partitioning) or a smaller context model variant for tail requests.
- For the streaming inter-token requirement (<150ms) we need to enable immediate flush on first token and set small internal micro-batch threshold (1-2 tokens) — that increases GPU overhead but preserves latency.
- Concurrency: sustaining 200 concurrent short requests will be dominated by token generation time. We should simulate with their RTTs (35/55ms) included. I recommend running a 30-minute soak at 200 concurrent, then 5x 60s bursts to 400 to capture the tail.
- Measurement: collect end-to-end from synthetic clients (browser RTT + provider time) and also provider-side times (service time, queue wait, kernel exec) so we can attribute p95/p99 to network vs provider.

I can spin up the hosted test with these parameters — need a heads-up on the model size they plan to use (we should mirror their production model). Also attaching a short benchmark we ran last month (redwood-hosted-latency-benchmarks-202602.pdf).

-Dev
